entities.name: PMID:27505193
observations: In 514 healthy adults inoculated with rhinovirus and monitored for 5 days, disadvantaged-background African Americans high in conscientiousness had better education, fewer depressive symptoms, and better close-relationship quality, but greater likelihood of developing illness after inoculation (p=.03).
European Americans showed better psychosocial outcomes with conscientiousness but no corresponding infection-risk association.

entities.name: PMID:32597677
observations: In rural African Americans followed from childhood to age 27, high planful self-control predicted college graduation and better psychological adjustment, while greater adolescent poverty among high-self-control participants predicted more metabolic-syndrome components and insulin resistance.

entities.name: PMID:27940737
observations: Critical commentary identified important unresolved questions about the skin-deep resilience construct among disadvantaged Black populations.

entities.name: Viral challenge finding
observations: Rhinovirus inoculation provided experimental evidence that a trait linked to psychosocial success can coincide with greater acute respiratory illness susceptibility in disadvantaged-background African Americans.
